en.title: Maximum Primary Memory with Primaries No Smaller Than Backups
en.description:
An even number of servers form primary-backup pairs one to one, and in each pair the backup's memory must be ≤ the primary's memory. Maximize the total memory of all primaries; note that the direction of the inequality in this problem follows the statement text.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O and judging; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains an even n (2..200000), and the second line contains n memory values (1..10⁹).
en.explanation: Example 1: 3 and 4 are primaries, paired with 1 and 2, for a total of 7. Example 2: equality is allowed, so the primary memory is 8. Example 3: 9 and 10 are primaries and the two 2s are backups, for a total of 19.
hints: After sorting, choose the largest n/2 servers as primaries and the rest as backups.
